title: Console banner + status widget copy (regional impairment + planned failover tests) — working mock
content:
Context
- Console needs a consistent, low-noise way to communicate:
  (a) Real regional impairment / active failover
  (b) Planned controlled failover tests (“game days”) with limited blast radius
  (c) Post-event stabilization (when metrics are still elevated but traffic is routed)
- Goal: reduce support load + reduce customer confusion during automation (routing flips, redirects, retry-after).
- Non-goal: replace Status Page; Console should link out and provide account-specific context.

Assumptions (check with PM-512 + Comms playbook)
- Console will show:
  - Top-of-page banner (global, dismissible with rules)
  - “Service status” widget on Overview (sticky card)
  - Optional per-project/per-endpoint callout on endpoint details page
- Region naming: use customer-friendly region IDs (e.g., US East, EU West) vs internal (us-east-1, eu-west-1) unless settings toggled.
- Must support both Hosted API and Dedicated.
- Console should never promise exact failover times.

Copy principles
- Be explicit about whether this is:
  - Planned test
  - Live incident
  - Recovered/monitoring
- Avoid the words “outage” unless we have strong corroboration (SRE wants to avoid false-positive language).
- Provide 1–2 clear CTAs:
  - “View status page”
  - “View incident details” (if we have an incident ID / internal customer incident page)
  - “View recommended client actions” (retry/backoff guidance)
- Mention scope:
  - “Some requests” vs “Most requests” vs “A subset of tenants/endpoints”
  - Hosted vs Dedicated differentiation
- For Dedicated: if we can map to a specific pool, show the pool label and current routing.

---

UI: Banner variants (top of Console)

0) Default (no banner)
- No banner shown when: status=normal, no planned test window relevant to tenant, no active impairment.

1) Planned test window (scheduled) — shown only to impacted tenants
Banner severity: INFO (blue)
Title: “Planned regional failover test scheduled”
Body (short): “We will run a controlled routing test affecting {Primary Region} between {Start Time}–{End Time} {TZ}. You may see brief reconnects or elevated latency.”
Secondary line (optional): “No action is required. Recommended: ensure your client retries are idempotent and respect Retry-After.”
CTA 1: “What to expect” (links to docs page / in-Console modal)
CTA 2: “View status page” (links to planned maintenance entry)
Dismiss behavior:
- Dismiss allowed, but re-appears if test window changes by >15 min or severity changes.

Notes:
- Time localization: show user’s timezone, but also include UTC in hover.
- Only show when we’re within T-72h of scheduled window.

2) Planned test in progress — impacted tenants only
Banner severity: INFO (blue) or WARNING (yellow) if we detect elevated error rate
Title: “Controlled regional routing test in progress”
Body (short): “We are testing automated regional failover from {Primary Region} to {Failover Region}. Some requests may be redirected.”
If streaming product surface exists:
- Add line: “Streaming responses may briefly disconnect; clients should reconnect and resume with the same request id.”
CTAs:
- “View live test updates” (links to status page entry or internal updates page)
- “Client retry guidance” (docs)
Dismiss behavior:
- Dismiss allowed; auto-clears when test ends.

3) Regional impairment detected (investigating) — broader audience, only if corroborated
Banner severity: WARNING (yellow)
Title: “Degraded performance in {Region}”
Body (short): “We are investigating elevated error rates and latency impacting {Product Scope} in {Region}. Traffic may be routed to another region.”
Product Scope examples:
- Hosted: “Hosted API requests”
- Dedicated: “Dedicated deployments in pool {Pool Name}”
CTAs:
- “View status page”
- “View affected endpoints” (links to widget details)
Dismiss behavior:
- Dismiss allowed, but re-appears if severity escalates.

4) Failover automation active (routing changes executing)
Banner severity: WARNING (yellow) or ERROR (red) depending on impact
Title option A: “Failover in progress”
Title option B (more specific): “Routing traffic away from {Impaired Region}”
Body (short): “We are shifting traffic to maintain availability. You may see brief timeouts or redirected connections while routing updates propagate.”
Body (secondary): “If you receive Retry-After, back off and retry.”
CTAs:
- “View incident details” (if incident exists)
- “View status page”
Optional inline status chip: “Automation: Active”

5) Failover complete / monitoring
Banner severity: INFO (blue)
Title: “Traffic routed to {Failover Region} (monitoring)”
Body: “We have redirected traffic to maintain availability. We are monitoring recovery in {Impaired Region}. Some workloads may see higher latency.”
CTAs:
- “View incident details”
- “View regions & routing”
Dismiss:
- Dismiss allowed; re-appears if rollback occurs.

6) Resolved
Banner severity: SUCCESS (green) — optional (debate: should we show success banners?)
Title: “Regional issue resolved”
Body: “Service has recovered in {Region}. Routing has returned to normal.”
CTAs:
- “View incident summary”
Auto-expire:
- Hide after 24 hours.

7) Dedicated data residency constraint (special case)
When we cannot fail over due to residency/contract settings.
Banner severity: ERROR (red)
Title: “Regional impairment affecting your deployment”
Body: “Your deployment is restricted to {Region} due to data residency or configuration. Failover to another region is not enabled.”
Body (secondary): “We are working to restore service. Contact support if you need to discuss multi-region options.”
CTAs:
- “Contact support”
- “View status page”

---

Widget: “Service status” card (Overview)

Widget states
A) Normal
- Header: “Service status”
- Subtext: “All systems operational.”
- Region line: “Primary region: {Region}. Failover region: {Region}.” (only if configured)
- Small link: “View status history”

B) Planned test scheduled
- Header: “Planned test”
- Subtext: “Controlled regional failover test scheduled {Start}–{End}.”
- Details expandable:
  - “Scope: Hosted API | Dedicated pool {Pool}”
  - “Expected impact: brief redirects, streaming reconnects, elevated latency.”
  - “Success criteria: no sustained elevated 5xx; failover within target window.” (careful: don’t publish internal numbers)
- Link: “What to expect”

C) Degraded performance / incident
- Header: “Degraded performance” (yellow)
- Subtext: “Elevated error rates/latency in {Region}.”
- Details:
  - “Current routing: {Primary}->{Failover} (partial)” or “{Primary}->{Failover} (complete)” or “No failover (restricted)”
  - “Impacted products: Chat completions / Embeddings / Streaming” (only if we can confidently map)
  - “Started: {Timestamp}”
- Links:
  - “View status page”
  - “View incident details” (if available)

D) Failover in progress
- Header: “Failover in progress”
- Subtext: “Routing updates are propagating.”
- Details:
  - “Automation mode: {Dry-run | Approved automation | Fully automated}” (maybe internal-only? keep behind admin flag)
  - “Recommended actions: respect Retry-After; retry with same request id; avoid aggressive parallel retries.”

E) Monitoring
- Header: “Monitoring” (blue)
- Subtext: “Traffic is routed to {Failover Region}. We are monitoring recovery.”
- Detail: “Some workloads may have higher latency due to capacity headroom.” (avoid too much detail)

---

In-Console modal: “What to expect” (planned test)

Title: “Planned regional failover test: what to expect”
Body:
- “This is a controlled test of our automated regional failover systems.”
- “During the window, some traffic will be redirected from {Primary Region} to {Failover Region}.”
- “Possible customer-visible symptoms (expected):
  - Brief increase in tail latency
  - Short burst of 5xx/timeouts during routing propagation
  - Streaming disconnects (clients should reconnect)
  - Responses with Retry-After during overload protection”
- “What we recommend:
  - Implement retries with exponential backoff
  - Make requests idempotent (use request IDs)
  - For streaming: reconnect on disconnect and resume the request”
- “Where to follow updates:
  - Status page
  - Console banner
  - Support for enterprise customers”
Footer:
- “Questions? Contact support.”

---

Edge cases / rules (notes for engineering + PM)
- Don’t show planned test banner to tenants not in scope (avoid trust erosion).
- If we have both “planned test” and “real impairment” simultaneously:
  - Real impairment wins (banner replaces planned test banner).
- Avoid flapping banners:
  - Introduce minimum display duration 10 min unless severity increases.
- Dismiss persistence:
  - Persist per user for 24h for planned scheduled banner.
  - Do not allow permanent dismissal of active incident banner.
- When routing changes cause redirect across regions:
  - Provide quick link to “Client guidance for redirects/streaming reconnect.”

Open questions
- Can we reliably label product surfaces impacted (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) without false positives?
- Should “Failover complete” banner be shown, or rely on widget + status page only?
- Dedicated: what wording is acceptable for pool drain events vs routing failover? (SRE vs Dedicated product)
- Do we expose “Automation mode” to customers? Proposed: no, keep internal.

Post-game day notes (2026-01-15)
- Support tickets referenced streaming disconnect confusion; we should explicitly mention reconnect expectations in both planned and incident variants (see SUP-25322).
- Customers misread “degraded performance” as full outage; consider “Intermittent errors in {Region}” as alternative title.
- We need better timestamping: show “Started at” and “Last updated” to reduce ‘is this current?’ questions.

Proposed next iteration
- Create a copy matrix table (state x product x tier) and run through Comms playbook.
- Review language with Support (Dev Patel) + SRE (Rafael) before finalizing.
- Align with DES-187 component constraints (character limits, CTA slots).
